A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoPart work, and all 11 pages of each are readable, including equations, figures, tables and references. Neither contains an appendix; supplementary material mentioned in the text is absent from both supplied files.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoPart generation results, quantitative comparisons in Table 1, a 51-participant user study in Table 2, and ablations in Figures 7–8.

after.justification: v2 retains the original generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, user-study outcomes and ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same geometric/image part latents, mutual and global guidance, bounding-box conditioning, refinement, training losses and editing procedure.

E1.justification: Both use the same PartVerse data and retain whole-object and part generation, editing, articulated-object and mini-scene demonstrations. No dataset, domain or evaluated scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Shap-E, Unique3D, CraftMan, Rodin and Trellis; Table 2 retains Rodin and PartGen. SALAD remains the qualitative comparator in Figure 4. Citation renumbering does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Both retain the CLIP/ULIP metrics, Flux.1 generation of conditioning images, half part-aware test cases and 51 user-study participants. Reported training settings, including batch size 1 and maximum eight parts, are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 7–8 retain the same global-guidance and refinement ablations, testing part coherence and the contribution of geometric guidance. Application examples are also unchanged; no new supplementary analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both report the same point-estimate and preference-percentage summaries. Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: All scores, preference percentages and timings in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. For example, CoPart retains part-aware scores of 0.1607, 0.1768 and 0.1355, and user preferences of 54.9% and 60.8%. Qualitative examples and ablation findings also match.

T1.justification: The representation definitions and Equations 1–13 are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: contextual part latents, synchronized generation through mutual guidance, controllable part generation and the PartVerse dataset. Their scientific scope and performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of global guidance and refinement are unchanged. Section 7 retains the limitation that incorrect user-provided bounding boxes can cause mesh clipping, alongside the same proposed future work.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the project address from hkdsc.github.io/project/copart to copart3d.github.io. This updates access information; implementation, hardware and data-processing disclosures otherwise match. The PDFs do not establish changed code or data availability.

R1.justification: v2 removes Raffel et al.'s unified text-to-text transformer paper, listed as reference 40 in v1 without a body citation. Remaining works match after renumbering, and the related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 removes one email address from the author contact line and updates the version/date header. Section order and substantive prose remain unchanged, with minor text reflow and citation renumbering.

P2.justification: Figures 4–5 use more compact arrangements, and text, Table 2 and Figure 7 shift within the layout. Both retain the same eight figures, two tables and visual examples, without substantive changes to captions or table structure.

improvement.justification: The scientific explanation, experimental evidence, claims and limitations remain unchanged. The project-address update, removal of an unused reference and contact address, and modest layout adjustments leave the paper's substantive clarity and evidential support essentially the same.
